evals.name: feature-ticket-from-brief-with-conflict
evals.prompt: Draft the M1 ticket for the reservation expiry work from the tech brief in evals/files/reservation-ttl-brief.md. The repo is inventory-service, the epic is PROJ-400, and the schema change ticket is PROJ-402. Just show me the draft in chat, do not create anything in Jira.
evals.expected_output: A single ticket draft in chat. Summary carries a scope prefix and M1. Body starts with a bolded Acceptance Criteria section, then Description with the spec link and a Blocked by sentence naming the schema change ticket, then Technical Notes beginning with 'Repo: inventory-service.' and per-file bullets. The default TTL conflict between section 2 (900 seconds) and section 5 (1800 seconds) is called out as an open question, not silently resolved.
expectations: The summary starts with a bracketed scope tag such as [Backend] and includes 'M1:'
The summary contains no priority marker (P0, P1, P2, Sev, Severity)
The body's first bolded section heading is Acceptance Criteria, appearing before Description and Technical Notes
A bolded Description section follows Acceptance Criteria and contains a 'Blocked by' sentence that names PROJ-402
A bolded Technical Notes section is last and its first line is 'Repo: inventory-service.'
The Acceptance Criteria bullets contain no file paths (no bullet contains a slash-separated path or a .java/.py filename)
At least one Acceptance Criteria bullet names the metric inventory.reservation_released and its tags
At least one Acceptance Criteria bullet covers two sweepers releasing the same reservation exactly once, or an equivalent idempotency check
The draft explicitly flags the 900 vs 1800 second default TTL inconsistency between the storage and API sections and asks which is correct, rather than picking one
The draft states the issue type is Task and the parent is PROJ-400
TTL is defined at its first use in the ticket body as 'TTL (time to live)' or 'time to live (TTL)'

The prose follows Simplified Technical English: no sentence exceeds 25 words, sentences name the agent in active voice (no 'is released', 'are published', 'gets rejected' constructions), and instructions in Technical Notes start with a verb
Nothing was created in Jira; no createJiraIssue call was made

evals.name: hygiene-ticket-from-findings
evals.prompt: Turn the findings in evals/files/dependency-findings.md into a ticket under our hygiene epic PROJ-10. Draft it here first; I'll tell you when to file it.
evals.expected_output: A hygiene-shaped ticket: one intro paragraph, then Acceptance Criteria, then Technical Notes, with no Description section. The summary ends with 'in billing-worker'. Technical Notes say to leave config-core and bus-client alone and why. The RetryPolicy behavior bug is kept out of this ticket and noted as tracked separately.
expectations: The summary starts with a bracketed scope tag and ends with 'in billing-worker'
The body opens with a plain intro paragraph (no heading) before the first bolded section
The body contains bolded Acceptance Criteria and Technical Notes sections and no Description section
An Acceptance Criteria bullet lists the dependency coordinates to be removed from worker/pom.xml
An Acceptance Criteria bullet requires the service to start and tests or CI to pass
An Acceptance Criteria bullet requires the minor version bump from 3.4.0 to 3.5.0
Technical Notes say to leave config-core and bus-client in place because they are loaded reflectively
Technical Notes mention that javax.annotation-api 1.3.2 remains transitively via jersey-client and that this is expected
The RetryPolicy InterruptedException bug is excluded from the acceptance criteria and described as tracked separately or to be filed on its own
The draft states Task type and parent PROJ-10

The prose follows Simplified Technical English: no sentence exceeds 25 words, sentences name the agent in active voice (no 'is released', 'are published', 'gets rejected' constructions), and instructions in Technical Notes start with a verb
Nothing was created in Jira

evals.name: split-epic-across-repos
evals.prompt: We're adding a 'snooze until' timestamp to support cases. The API lives in case-service (Java) and the settings form lives in web-app. The column snooze_until DATETIME NULL has to be added by the DB team first; that request is DBA-77. Break this into tickets for epic PROJ-500 and show me the drafts.
evals.expected_output: Two or more atomic drafts, one per repo (case-service, web-app), each with the three sections in order. The case-service ticket is blocked by DBA-77 with a note to create a real Blocks link. The web-app ticket is blocked by the case-service ticket. No ticket spans both repos.
expectations: At least two separate ticket drafts are produced
No single draft's Technical Notes name both case-service and web-app as its repo
Each draft's Technical Notes begin with a 'Repo:' line naming exactly one repo
Each draft's sections appear in the order Acceptance Criteria, Description, Technical Notes
The case-service draft's Description contains 'Blocked by' and names DBA-77
The web-app draft is described as blocked by the case-service ticket
The response says to create real Jira Blocks links for the dependencies, not only text
The case-service draft's Acceptance Criteria include a POST without snooze_until leaving the existing value unchanged, or an equivalent no-regression check
The web-app draft's summary uses a [Frontend] scope tag

The prose follows Simplified Technical English: no sentence exceeds 25 words, sentences name the agent in active voice (no 'is released', 'are published', 'gets rejected' constructions), and instructions in Technical Notes start with a verb
